newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Czech c.bank head says crown fall normal.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank head says crown fall normal.

text.p: Czech National Bank governor Josef Tosovsky said Friday's sharp weakening of the crown was "a normal movement" and that the bank would only intervene to eliminate huge volatility.

"I think it is a normal movement," he told reporters, adding the currency was in a managed float. "So we would only try to eliminate huge volatility and this would be our policy. Otherwise if there would be new trends, we would certainly not defend our currency to go to new levels, which would be more in line with fundamentals," Tosovsky said.

The crown weakened sharply early on Friday following attacks on the currency from London, dealers said. They said the selling was partly spurred by fears of the economic costs of major flooding in the northern and eastern parts of the Czech Republic.
The crown opened near 18.8 against the mark but quickly fell to about 18.96, where it steadied.
But asked at a news conference at the second Central and Eastern European Economic Conference about the impact of the flooding on GDP and other indicators, Tosovsky said it was too early to say.

The Czech parliament approved on Thursday a government proposal to release five billion crowns in privatisation proceeds for a flood relief programme. Earlier in the day, the government approved issuance of up to five billion crowns in domestic bonds for flood relief.
"Probably even more support will be needed in the future," Tosovsky told the news conference.
The central bank allowed the crown to float on May 27 after a wave of speculative selling by investors alarmed at widening current account and trade deficits.
